title: Staged kernel virtualization and architecture fingerprinting for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce onboarding friction and tail latency variance by introducing an architecture fingerprinting phase plus a staged 'kernel virtualization' path that allows the compile+pin pipeline to safely try alternate kernel variants (e.g., grouped-attention kernels, GQA optimizations, MoE expert routing kernels) without impacting live traffic.

Motivation: Current onboarding pins a single kernel profile after a short validation window; for complex topologies (GQA, MoE with sharded experts) this produces oscillating latency and occasional correctness edge cases when kernel selection is brittle. We need a safer, observable approach that can trial multiple compiled kernels per model version and surface deterministic fallbacks while keeping rollback fast and auditable.

Scope: Implement fingerprinting kicker during model ingestion, add a staged kernel virtualization layer in runtime that can route % of traffic to candidate kernels, add control-plane hooks for pin publishing and expiration, and extend the performance-profile publisher to record multi-variant metrics. This ticket covers engineering changes (runtime routing, telemetry, profile schema), integration with the model-onboarder, and a small Console UX to show candidate kernel trials for a model version.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprinting step computes a concise architecture fingerprint (string) and stores with model metadata
Runtime supports declaring up to 3 candidate kernel profiles per model version and can route traffic to candidates via rollout percentages
Profiling pipeline aggregates per-candidate latency/throughput/oom/correctness metrics for 24h and surfaces regressions in outputs
Publish workflow emits a single canonical pin only after explicit approval or when candidate trial reaches SLA thresholds
Rollback to baseline kernel must be possible within 30s via control-plane API
E2E test simulates a 100k token workload across MHA/GQA/MoE models and shows improved P99 stability vs current baseline
notes: Compliance: candidate trials must not expose customer data; all telemetry uses redacted ids
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike showing >2x P99 variance for a 32B MoE when pinned to single kernel variant.
2025-02-12 Lucas Nguyen: Spike implemented architecture fingerprinting and a tiny router shim that can split by trace header. Local perf indicates candidate routing overhead ~0.4ms per request.
2025-02-14 Design review (Marta Oliveira): UX mockups look good, but request that console shows candidate health (OOMs per hour) and not only latency. Added acceptance criteria.

2025-02-16 Security review (Raj Singh): Telemetry must be hashed and sampled at 1% by default for public clusters. Marked security_review_required=false but followup ticket may be required for Private deployments.

2025-02-18 Engineering note (Lucas Nguyen): Integrating with kernel-autotuner requires a small adapter to translate autotuner scores into candidate weights. Prototype adapter in PR #7123; need product decision on automatic promotion thresholds.

2025-02-19 PM feedback (Hannah Lee): Recommend a 24h minimum trial window for high-variance MoE workloads and ability to extend trial to 72h for enterprise customers. Added to acceptance criteria discussion.

2025-02-20 Lucas Nguyen: Canary run started in staging against model: redwood/moe-32b-v2. Candidate A (grouped-attn-optim) at 10% shows 12% lower median latency but 3% more OOMs; instrumenting automated alert to pause candidate when OOM delta > 1% over 1h.
implementation_notes: Runtime shim should be lightweight: decisions made pre-compile on first-request path and cached in instance-local config
Candidate profiles stored in profile store with TTL and explicit 'promote' flag; promotion triggers publish-pin job that creates immutable pin entry
Telemetry keys: candidate_id, model_version, kernel_variant, p50,p95,p99,oom_count,gen_error_rate. All keys redacted as required.
Control-plane API: POST /models/:id/versions/:v/candidates -> {kernel_variant, weight, reason}; PATCH to adjust weights or to promote/abort
E2E test harness: reuse existing perf harness (ENG-54821) but extend to support multi-candidate traffic splits and correctness diffing
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased complexity in runtime routing could add latency. Mitigation: keep decision logic in hot path under 1ms and offload heavy telemetry to async pipeline.
Risk: Candidate kernels may regress correctness. Mitigation: require deterministic output diffs for a sample of requests and abort on regression thresholds.
Risk: Private/on-prem customers may lack autoscaler to handle candidate-induced OOMs. Mitigation: default low weights (<=5%) for trials in Private unless customer opts in.
Risk: Explosion of stored profiles. Mitigation: TTL + LRU on profile store and compacted representation for candidate metrics
